Does stock-service track BATCH / LOT and EXPIRY per store?

yes → build the full plan
expiry on SKU only → FEFO + goods-receipt date + shelf life
 = estimated expiry. Say it is an estimate.
no expiry data → NOT VIABLE as specified. Fall back to a
 slow-mover / dead-stock markdown driven by
 days-of-cover. Still useful. Still honest.

or a different plan entirely." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="250" width="420" x="40" y="90" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="inp" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;fontFamily=Courier New;" value="days_left = expiry − today
on_hand = units of this batch at this store
baseline_demand = Chronos-2 over days_left
uplift(discount) = I01 elasticity, near-expiry context
expected_sold = f(baseline, uplift, shelf position,
 competing full-price stock)
expected_waste = max(0, on_hand − expected_sold)

recovered_margin(d) =
 expected_sold × (price×(1−d) − cost)
 − expected_waste × cost

choose d AND the day to apply it" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="220" width="430" x="20" y="44" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c2" parent="calc" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;fontStyle=1" value="Two behaviours fall out of the maths:
• discount EARLY and SHALLOW beats late and deep
• sometimes the answer is DO NOT DISCOUNT — a model
 that recommends no action is doing its job" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="430" x="20" y="274" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="opt" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;" value="Markdown optimizer (OR-Tools, CPU)

store-level constraints:
max % of assortment on markdown at once
category markdown ladders · min margin
label-printing capacity · items per store per day

CATEGORY BLOCKLIST — never mark down where
discounting near-expiry is restricted
(health / pharma / infant formula), reviewed by compliance" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="470" x="520" y="490" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="wl" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;fontStyle=1" value="Store worklist (POS / tablet, early morning)

print labels

declarative offer schema + validator" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="80" width="360" x="1050" y="310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="fb" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;" value="feedback loop

and per discount depth → re-fit the uplift curve monthly" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="360" x="1050" y="430" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kpi" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=34;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=#fffdf5;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontStyle=1;fontSize=12;fontColor=#8a6d1e;" value="KPIs — this is the pitch" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="320" width="360" x="1050" y="560" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="k1" parent="kpi" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1" value="Write-off value per week — before vs after

guards against discounting what would have sold" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="46" width="330" x="15" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="k4" parent="kpi" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;" value="Markdown ROI = recovered margin ÷ discount cost
the number a CFO asks for" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="46" width="330" x="15" y="194" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="k5" parent="kpi" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1" value="Compliance rate — recommended markdowns
actually applied in store. Predicts everything else." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="46" width="330" x="15" y="248" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="why" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f9f9f9;strokeColor=#999999;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;dashed=1;verticalAlign=middle;" value="Why this is the strongest "green" idea available: waste reduction and margin recovery are the SAME action, so nobody is asked to spend money to be virtuous.
The measurement is unambiguous — write-off value is already an accounting line, and before/after shows up in weeks.
Only claim what is measured: report VND and units; report CO₂e only with a citable factor. Sources: InsiderOne #9, #5 · NetSuite (perishables) · Innowise (green retailing)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="100" width="970" x="40" y="700" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ea" edge="1" div.div:
WEEK-1 GATE — ask this before anything else
Does stock-service track BATCH / LOT and EXPIRY per store?
yes → build the full plan
expiry on SKU only → FEFO + goods-receipt date + shelf life
= estimated expiry. Say it is an estimate.
no expiry data → NOT VIABLE as specified. Fall back to a
slow-mover / dead-stock markdown driven by
days-of-cover. Still useful. Still honest.
This one question decides whether I02 is a 12-day extension of I01
or a different plan entirely.

div.div:
days_left = expiry − today
on_hand = units of this batch at this store
baseline_demand = Chronos-2 over days_left
uplift(discount) = I01 elasticity, near-expiry context
expected_sold = f(baseline, uplift, shelf position,
competing full-price stock)
expected_waste = max(0, on_hand − expected_sold)
recovered_margin(d) =
expected_sold × (price×(1−d) − cost)
− expected_waste × cost
choose d AND the day to apply it

div.div:
Why this is the strongest "green" idea available: waste reduction and margin recovery are the SAME action, so nobody is asked to spend money to be virtuous.
The measurement is unambiguous — write-off value is already an accounting line, and before/after shows up in weeks.
Only claim what is measured: report VND and units; report CO₂e only with a citable factor. Sources: InsiderOne #9, #5 · NetSuite (perishables) · Innowise (green retailing).
